paragraphs: Rabbi Pinchas, son of Rabbi Chananyah.

In Hyman’s account of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 4:1, Pinchas’s father, Rabbi Chananyah, responds to Rabbi Chagai, and Rabbi Pinchas son of Rabbi Chananyah answers his objection. In Shekalim chapter 2 [supplied כה״א; compare 2:1], he disagrees with Rabbi Abba Mari.

notes.text: The extra kaf in כה״א and the intermediate referent of “his objection” remain unresolved. The father-son relationship is explicit in the notice.

The saved whole Venice Shekalim2:1 scalar names Rabbi Pinchas bei Rabbi Chananyah and Rabbi Abba Mari with opposing views, superseding the earlier exact-spelling nonmatch. These actual full titles support the connected heading names; uninspected Chagai remains R'. The supplied chapter2 locator כה״א remains visible beside the named2:1 match, without printed-letter history proof. The father responding to Chagai and the son answering his objection remain Hyman’s Shabbat4:1 report; the new Shekalim paragraph does not settle that pronoun’s antecedent.

The printed notice crosses pp. 1014–1015 of volume III and retains כה״א in its Shekalim reference. In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 4:1, Rabbi Chagai raises the objection about a grain store. Rabbi Chananyah explains the rule in terms of mice. Rabbi Pinchas bei Rabbi Chanina challenges that explanation, and the passage says Rabbi Chagai’s objection stands. This gives a more specific sequence and a different patronymic spelling from Hyman’s report. In Shekalim 2:1, Pinchas bei Chananyah and Abba Mari offer different criteria, and the passage leaves their individual positions unspecified.
